validity.recommendation: merge into P3962 (same East–West pipeline); P3966 is a network/roll-up buffer row, not a distinct physical pipe
validity.researcher_notes: P3966 and P3962 are the same entity. Both carry the identical PipelineName 'East–West Gas Pipeline (Saudi Arabia)', the identical route (Abqaiq/Eastern Province -> Yanbu/Al Madinah), point to the EXACT same gem.wiki page, and in the harvested wiki_citations.json carry an IDENTICAL citation list (the AlHadath YouTube clip, the pgjonline $7.5B-loan story, fanack.com, and the americas.aramco MGS article). In the live GGIT CSV (snapshot 20260619) P3962 is SegmentName='Main Line', LengthKnown=1200 km, Diameter=48, StartYear1=1978, Capacity blank; P3966 is SegmentName='SYSTEM/NETWORK INFO', LengthKnown=821 km, Diameter blank, Status blank, Capacity=5.20 mill.Sm3/day, and its Background cell is the placeholder 'Nagwa: No pdate'. The 'SYSTEM/NETWORK INFO' segment label plus a placeholder Background and a divergent length/capacity is the signature of a GEM network roll-up / buffer row that double-counts the physical line already recorded as P3962's 'Main Line'. Recommend merging P3966 into P3962 (or deleting it) rather than maintaining two rows for one pipeline. NOTE the secondary classification concern below — the merge target itself is misclassified.

validity.recommendation: reclassify / likely remove from GGIT — the Abqaiq–Yanbu East–West corridor is the crude Petroline plus a parallel NGL line, not a dry-gas transmission trunk; the NGL line belongs in GOIT, not GGIT
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records this as Fuel='Gas', PipelineType='transmission' in the gas tracker (GGIT). Independent sources show the Abqaiq->Yanbu 'East–West' corridor is fundamentally the crude-oil Petroline (1,200 km, ~5 mb/d design crude capacity, two lines 48in/56in) WITH a separate parallel natural-gas-LIQUIDS (NGL) line (~300 kb/d) — not a dry natural-gas transmission pipeline. ENR (enr.com, verified, contains 'crude'/'NGL'/'East-West'/'Yanbu') and geoconversation.org (verified, contains 'crude'/'Abqaiq'/'East-West') both describe crude + parallel NGL on this exact route; europeanbusinessmagazine.com corroborates (verified, contains 'NGL'/'Yanbu'/'crude'). Aramco's own MGS material (the wiki's source 4) describes gas moving EAST/inland on the Master Gas System, not a dry-gas trunk running west to Yanbu. I found NO independent evidence of a dry-gas TRANSMISSION pipeline on the Abqaiq->Yanbu route. The capacity 5.20 mill.Sm3/day is unsourced and inconsistent with the crude/NGL liquids design of this corridor. Bottom line: the entry is the wrong commodity/type for GGIT — the parallel liquids line is NGL (a GOIT entity), the trunk is crude (already tracked as GEM's 'East-West Crude Oil Pipeline'). Strong existence-as-a-dry-gas-line doubt; recommend reclassifying or removing from the gas tracker after the P3966->P3962 merge.

summary: P3966 East–West Gas (SA): DUPLICATE of P3962 (same name/route/wiki/citations; P3966 is the SYSTEM/NETWORK-INFO roll-up row) AND misclassified — the Abqaiq–Yanbu corridor is the crude Petroline + parallel NGL line, not a dry-gas transmission trunk; recommend merge into P3962 then reclassify/remove from GGIT.
